hero.h1: Sewer Rodding in Lincoln Park, Chicago
hero.sub: Water at the basement floor drain, a garden unit toilet that gurgles or every fixture in the building slowing down. That's the main line. We rod it clear and show you what caused it on camera. Our office is on Diversey Parkway.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber feeding the cable from a drum rodding machine into an outdoor sewer cleanout in a front yard

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Signs the Main Line Is Blocked
blocks.intro: In a Lincoln Park home or building:

tiles.body: It's the lowest opening, so it shows first.
When units upstairs run water, it ends up downstairs.
They share one line to the street.
Roots in old clay grow back each year.

blocks.h2: What Blocks Main Lines in Lincoln Park
blocks.intro: Old pipe and dense living make for familiar clogs here.

items.body: Parkway trees send roots into joints along the lateral.
In a multi-unit building, every kitchen drains to the same line.
More bathrooms on one line means more chances for a clog.
If roots return in months, [hydro jetting](/chicago-lincoln-park/hydro-jetting) or a [repair](/chicago-lincoln-park/sewer-repair) lasts longer.

blocks.intro: Clear the line, then show you why.

steps.body: In the basement, the front yard or under the stoop.
Cleared to the city sewer and checked on video.
And options if we find damage.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding in a Condo Building
blocks.body: When a shared main line clogs, every unit in the building feels it, but only the lowest one floods. In a Lincoln Park condo building, the fastest fix starts with one call: someone with access to the basement cleanout. We clear the line, record it on camera and send the footage, so the board can decide whether routine rodding is enough or a repair belongs in the budget.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Where is the cleanout in a Chicago two-flat?
items.preview: Usually in the basement near the front wall.
items.answer: Usually in the basement near the front of the building, sometimes outside near the stoop. Some older buildings don't have an accessible one, and adding one helps.

items.q: How often should the main line be rodded?
items.preview: Yearly if roots are a known problem.
items.answer: If roots have blocked the line before, once a year is common.

items.q: Can you rod a line from inside a condo unit?
items.answer: Main line work is done from the building's cleanout. If only your unit's branch is clogged, we can clear it from inside.

items.q: Is rodding safe for an old clay line?
items.answer: Yes, with a cutter sized for the pipe. The camera afterward shows its condition.

items.q: Can you send the video to our association?
items.answer: Yes. We can share it with the board or management.

items.q: How much does sewer rodding cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the cleanout is, the length of the line and what's blocking it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
